physical_harm: Deceased suffered multiple cranio-cerebral injuries resulting in death; witness also suffered grievous injuries
premeditation_planning: Yes, the appellants came armed and expressed determination to kill the deceased
motive: Acquittal of the deceased in a criminal prosecution at the behest of appellant
key_evidence_accepted: The number of injuries on the head of the deceased is sufficient to conclude the nature of murderous assault made by all the appellants. The credible ocular evidence available, including the testimony of PW-1 Lalbahadur Sastri, establishes the intention to cause death and the motive.
witness_credibility: The credibility and reliability of PW-1 as an eye witness are established. The court emphasized that the number of injuries on the deceased's head and the fact that PW-1 was present at the time of the assault supports his testimony. The court also found PW-2 and PW-3 to be reliable eye-witnesses.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: Not stated; Trial judgment: 30.08.2010; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: May 22, 2017
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Gopal Shankaranarayan, Anil Kumar Mishra-I, Ranjith B. Marar, Lakshmesh S. Karnath, Deepak Anand, Ms. Lakshmi K.; Counsel for the State: Ms. Nithya, M. Yogesh Kanna, Utkarsh Srivastav, Partha Sarathi, A Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered soon after the occurrence; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants mercilessly assaulted the deceased on the head with weapons, resulting in his death. The credibility and reliability of PW-1 as an eye witness were established, and the number of injuries on the deceased's head indicated a murderous assault. The failure to produce the first injury report of the witness was noted but not fatal to the prosecution case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no motive for Balasubramanian to commit the assault, and that the witnesses were related to the deceased and thus interested witnesses. They also questioned the credibility of the eye-witness accounts and the reliability of the injury reports.
legal_principle_applied: Criminal jurisprudence attaches great weightage to the evidence of a person injured in the same occurrence, as it presumes that he was speaking the truth unless shown otherwise.
precedent_relied_upon: Brahm Swaroop v. State of U.P. (2011) 6 SCC 288; Pattipati Venkaiah v. State of A.P (1985) 4 SCC 80
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the indiscriminate and repeated assault on the deceased's head with weapons, which reflected the individual intention of each appellant to ensure the death of the deceased. The intention to cause death, along with motive, was established.
other_sentence_order: The appeals were dismissed, and the appellants' bail bonds were cancelled. They were directed to surrender forthwith for serving out their remaining period of sentence.
